proof_summary: Let \(B=\lfloor n^{1/4}\rfloor+1\) and \(T=B^3\), and take all integers up to \(T\) together with all primes up to \(n\): an integer whose largest prime factor exceeds \(B\) is that prime times a factor at most \(T\), while a \(B\)-smooth integer can be split into two factors at most \(T\), so this set has size at most \(T+\pi(n)\). The estimates \(4^m\le m\binom{2m}{m}\le m(2m)^{\pi(2m)}\), together with logarithmic growth, imply eventually \(\pi(2m)\ge m^{3/4}\), hence \(T\le 32\pi(n)\); the remaining finite range is bounded separately.
